name: Tep Pranam
significance: A Buddhist terrace inside Angkor Thom whose colossal seated Buddha is assembled from sandstone blocks and reached by a 75-metre laterite causeway from the east. The wooden hall that once sheltered the image has vanished, leaving the cruciform foundation and the boundary markers of its terrace.

name: Wat Langka
deity: Buddha (bronze Buddha images enshrined in the stupa, facing the four directions)
significance: One of the older Theravada monasteries of Phnom Penh, founded in 1442 by Ponhea Yat as a refuge, a repository for the Tripitaka and a meeting place for Khmer and Sri Lankan monks. It escaped destruction under the Khmer Rouge because the regime used the compound as a storage warehouse.
story: Its name commemorates the gathering of Khmer and Sri Lankan monks, tied to the account of Buddhaghosa copying the scriptures brought from Sri Lanka.

name: Thottuva Dhanwanthari Temple
deity: Dhanwanthari (Adi Dhanwanthari), the physician form of Vishnu
significance: Described as the only temple in Kerala with Dhanwanthari as its principal deity, its east-facing image standing close to six feet and holding the vessel of amrita. The shrine belongs to the Koramboor Mana family and is run by the Sree Dhanwanthari Moorthi Seva Trust.
story: A Namboodiri Brahmin cursed by Shankaracharya for withholding hospitality is said to have been consoled at this spot by the voice of Dhanwanthari, and the place where he set down his umbrella is still called Kudappadom.

name: Tiruvaneshwar Temple
deity: Shiva as Tiruvaneshwar (Gajaranyeswarar / Karivananathar), consort Kamakshi Ambal
significance: A Shiva temple at Ranganathapuram in the Thiruvaiyaru taluk of Thanjavur district, where the deity carries the elephant-forest names Gajaranyeswarar and Karivananathar. The Kanchi Kamakoti pontiff Chandrashekharendra Saraswati is recorded to have stayed a week here in meditation.

name: Thrikkavu Temple
deity: Durga Bhagavathy, worshipped in the three forms of Parvati, Lakshmi and Saraswati
builtDisplay: dating unrecorded; restored after Tipu Sultan's raid
significance: A Durga temple at Ponnani whose idol was destroyed when Tipu Sultan's forces turned the shrine into an ammunition depot; the Zamorin afterwards had it restored.
story: It is counted among the 108 Durga shrines said to have been consecrated by Parashurama, and its name is traced to the old forest tract called Thrikkani Kaadu.

name: Talesvara Siva Temple
place: Kedar Gouri road, Old Town, Bhubaneswar
deity: Shiva (lingam set in a circular yonipitha)
significance: A small rekha deul on the Kedar Gouri road in old Bhubaneswar, a short walk from the Parasuramesvara temple, believed to have been founded in the 8th century. It stood ruined until the Odisha state archaeology department repaired it, and it remains in private hands.

name: Tirthesvara Siva Temple
deity: Shiva (lingam set in a circular yonipitha)
significance: A west-facing Shiva shrine on the Talabazar road that runs from Bindusagar towards the Lingaraja temple in old Bhubaneswar. Its architectural detail matches Ganga-period work, on which basis it is dated to about the 14th century, and it is still served by local priests.

name: Thottipal Bhagavati Temple
builtDisplay: dating unrecorded; renovated in the late 19th c.
significance: A Bhagavathy temple in Thrissur district that was wrecked during Tipu Sultan's campaigns and rebuilt in the late 1800s. It takes part in both the Arattupuzha Pooram and the Peruvanam Pooram.
story: It is counted among the 108 Devi shrines said to have been installed by Parashurama, and the goddess is held to be the sister of Urathammathiruvadi and of the Chathakudam Sastha.

name: Tirusoolanathar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Tirusulam on the south-western edge of Chennai, credited to the medieval Chola king Kulothunga I and later renovated, with inscriptions of the Chola and Pandya periods. A Tripurasundari image damaged during an invasion is kept beside the presiding deity.
story: Tradition speaks of a hidden passage beneath the temple leading to the nearby Pancha Pandava hills where the king had his palace, along which treasure is said to have been concealed.

name: Thrippara Shiva Kshetram
builtDisplay: said to be about 800 years old
significance: A Shiva temple at Vallicode in Pathanamthitta district reckoned to be some eight centuries old, unusual among the shrines nearby in that its sanctum stands in the open directly above the temple ghats.

name: Varasiddhi Vinayaka Temple
deity: Ganesha as Valampuri Varasiddhi Vinayakar, with his consort Siddhi
significance: A Ganesha temple near the beach at Besant Nagar in Chennai whose image was first worshipped on a site opposite the present one inside the CPWD quarters; the enlarged temple had its first kumbhabhishekam in April 1979. An auditorium and a goshala were added later, and music programmes mark Vinayaka Chaturthi.

name: Velleeswarar Temple, Mangadu
deity: Shiva as Velleeswarar (also called Sukreswara and Bhargaveswarar)
significance: One of the three principal temples of Mangadu on the western edge of Chennai, about two kilometres from the Kamakshi Amman temple, counted in the Navagraha circuit around the city as the shrine of Sukra and administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department.
story: Sukra, the planet Venus, is said to have worshipped Shiva here, which is why the deity is called Velleeswarar or Bhargaveswarar; the same tradition places Kamakshi's penance at Mangadu before her marriage to Shiva at Kanchipuram.

name: Puttingal Temple
significance: A Bhadrakali temple at Paravur in Kollam district whose Meena Bharani festival is known for its competitive fireworks. On 10 April 2016 an unauthorised display set off the stored fireworks, killing 114 people and injuring more than 350.
story: The temple is said to have been founded where the goddess made her presence felt on an ant hill, puttu in Malayalam, which gives the shrine its name.

name: Pattupurakkavu Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A Bhadrakali temple a kilometre north of Pandalam junction on the Thiruvananthapuram–Angamaly MC Road, with subsidiary shrines to Ganapathi and Shiva. It hosted the first Devi Bhagavatha Sathram held in Kerala, from 28 April to 7 May 2010.

name: Poruvazhy Peruviruthy Malanada Temple
deity: Mala Appooppan, the sankalpa murti of Duryodhana
significance: A hill shrine in Kollam district, rare in being dedicated to Duryodhana of the Mahabharata and in having neither an idol nor a sanctum, worship instead being offered through sankalpam. It is run by a committee drawn from seven territorial divisions.
story: Duryodhana, searching for the exiled Pandavas, is said to have been given toddy on this hill by an elderly Kurava woman, and, moved by the place and its people, to have worshipped Shiva there and endowed the shrine with farmland.

name: Punkunnam Seetha Ramaswamy Temple
deity: Rama with Sita, sharing a single pedestal; shrines to Lakshmana and Hanuman
significance: A Rama temple in the Pushpagiri agraharam at Punkunnam in Thrissur, built in 1899 by T. R. Ramachandra Iyer, a justice of the Cochin court, as his personal shrine. Rama and Sita share one pedestal, older Shiva and Ayyappan shrines stand in the same compound, and a 55-foot Hanuman statue was unveiled in April 2023.

name: Prasanna Venkatesa Perumal Temple, Saidapet
deity: Vishnu as Prasanna Venkata Narasimha, with Sridevi and Bhudevi
significance: A Vishnu temple at Saidapet in Chennai where the east-facing Prasanna Venkata Narasimha stands with Sridevi and Bhudevi. The article dates it to the 12th century and attributes its building to the Balija Chetty community under Vijayanagara rule; the Ramanuja Vijaya Vilasam hall, now the Ramanuja Koodam, was added in 1901.

name: Podhu Aavudayar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Parakkalakkottai near Pattukkottai in Thanjavur district, unusual in its hours: it opens only at midnight on Mondays and closes three or four hours later, with additional access on the morning of Thai Pongal.
story: Two sages, Vankobar and Mahakobar, are said to have argued over whether celibacy or married life was the higher path and, unable to settle it, asked Shiva to judge; he appeared to them at Parakkalakkottai and gave his verdict.
